com-ga-xoi-mo.name: Vietnamese Crispy Chicken with Egg Fried Rice
com-ga-xoi-mo.serving_basis: Four rice portions, each served with a piece of fried chicken and fresh vegetables.
com-ga-xoi-mo.description: Chicken is seasoned, gently poached and dried before frying until crisp. The poaching broth flavors the rice, which is cooled and stir-fried with egg; fresh cucumber, tomato, carrot and daikon balance the plate.
com-ga-xoi-mo.finished_dish: The chicken skin is crisp and golden with juicy, fully cooked meat. Garlic-and-egg rice stays separate and tender rather than dry.
com-ga-xoi-mo.serving: Plate the rice beside the chicken and serve hot with cucumber, tomato, pickled daikon and carrot, plus soy sauce or a sweet-sour fish sauce dip.
tips: Let the chicken cool and dry thoroughly before frying to reduce splatter and help the skin crisp.
Strain the poaching broth for the rice; cool the rice before adding egg so the grains do not clump.
Fry in batches without crowding the pan and check that the meat near the bone is cooked through.
search_terms: chicken with sticky rice fried in chicken fat
com-ga-xoi-mo.image_alt: Crispy poached chicken served with egg-fried rice, cucumber, tomato and pickled vegetables.
com-ga-xoi-mo.time_note: About 110 minutes including marinating and cooling; the rice can cook while the chicken dries.

ingredients.name: Chicken pieces
ingredients.notes: Use thighs, wings or half a chicken cut into portions.

ingredients.name: White rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cook with strained chicken broth.

ingredients.name: Chicken eggs
ingredients.notes: Beat and mix with cooled rice.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Finely chop; divide between the chicken marinade and rice.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Slice for the poaching broth.

ingredients.name: Scallion whites
ingredients.notes: Add to the chicken poaching pot.

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Use in the marinade or as a dip.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between the marinade and broth.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Adds mild sweetness to the marinade.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying; the amount absorbed by the food will be much lower.

ingredients.name: Cucumber
ingredients.notes: Slice for serving.

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.notes: Cut into wedges or slices.

ingredients.name: Carrot

ingredients.name: Daikon radish
ingredients.notes: Julienne, rinse and drain for serving fresh.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse the chicken, cut into serving pieces and pat dry. Mince the garlic, slice the ginger and wash the scallion whites.
Marinate the chicken with garlic, soy sauce, sugar and some of the salt for about 30 minutes, refrigerated.
Slice the cucumber and tomato; julienne the carrot and daikon, soak briefly in ice water, then drain for a crisp fresh side.

cooking_steps.instruction: Bring water to a gentle simmer with ginger, scallion whites and the remaining salt. Poach the chicken until just cooked, then drain and cool completely; reserve and strain the broth.
Heat oil in a deep pot. Fry the chicken in batches over medium heat until golden and crisp and cooked through near the bone; drain on a rack.
Cook the rice with the strained chicken broth, using the amount appropriate for the rice. Spread the cooked rice out to cool slightly.
Fry the remaining garlic in a little oil, add the rice and loosen the grains. Pour in the beaten egg and stir until it coats the rice and is just set.
Serve the egg rice with the fried chicken, fresh cucumber, tomato, carrot and daikon, with soy sauce or a preferred dipping sauce.

com-ga-xoi-mo.media_alt_text: Crispy poached chicken served with egg-fried rice, cucumber, tomato and pickled vegetables.

canh-ga-nhoi-com.name: Chicken Wings Stuffed with Young Green Rice
canh-ga-nhoi-com.serving_basis: Six stuffed wings served as a savory rice-meal dish for four.
canh-ga-nhoi-com.description: Deboned chicken wings are filled with pork paste, shiitake and young green rice, briefly steamed to set the filling, then coated with egg and more steamed rice before frying. The coating turns lightly crisp while keeping its fragrant, tender center.
canh-ga-nhoi-com.finished_dish: The wings hold their shape, the filling is cooked and cohesive, and the green-rice coating is fragrant and lightly golden rather than dark.
canh-ga-nhoi-com.serving: Serve hot with cucumber, fresh herbs and steamed rice. Rest the wings for a few minutes before cutting so the filling stays intact.
tips: Debone gently and leave the tip joint intact so the wing does not tear.
Divide the steamed rice between the filling and outer coating; do not overstuff because the filling expands slightly during steaming.
Cool the steamed wings and dry their surface before brushing with egg and coating with steamed rice.
Fry over medium heat so the wings cook through without darkening the rice coating.
search_terms: chicken wings with young green rice
canh-ga-nhoi-com.image_alt: Crisp chicken wings filled with young green rice, pork and shiitake mushrooms, served on a plate.
canh-ga-nhoi-com.time_note: About 65 minutes including deboning, stuffing, brief steaming and frying.

ingredients.name: Chicken wings
ingredients.notes: Debone while leaving the tip joint intact to retain the wing shape.

ingredients.name: Young green rice flakes
ingredients.notes: Divide into about 130 g for the filling and 70 g for the coating.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese pork paste
ingredients.notes: Keep chilled until mixing the filling.

ingredients.name: Dried shiitake
ingredients.notes: Soak until soft, squeeze dry and mince.

ingredients.name: Dried shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely mince.

ingredients.name: Egg yolks
ingredients.notes: Beat to coat the wings before rolling in steamed rice.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Use moderately because the pork paste is already seasoned.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Mix into the filling.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying; the amount absorbed will be lower.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Wash and use as garnish and accompaniment.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse the wings and carefully remove the bones, leaving the tip joint intact. Soak the shiitake until soft and mince it.
Mince the shallot; mix the pork paste with shiitake, shallot, fish sauce, pepper and about 130 g of the steamed rice.
Fill each wing with a moderate amount of stuffing, close the opening and arrange on a parchment-lined steamer tray.

cooking_steps.instruction: Steam the wings for about 10 minutes to set the filling. Remove, cool and pat the surface dry.
Beat the egg yolks. Brush them over the wings, then roll in the remaining steamed rice, pressing gently so the grains adhere.
Heat the oil over medium heat. Fry the wings in batches, turning until the coating is golden and the chicken is cooked through; drain.
Rest for a few minutes, then serve hot with cilantro, cucumber and steamed rice.

canh-ga-nhoi-com.media_alt_text: Crisp chicken wings filled with young green rice, pork and shiitake mushrooms, served on a plate.

chim-cau-bam-xuc-phong-tom.name: Minced Pigeon with Shrimp Crackers
chim-cau-bam-xuc-phong-tom.serving_basis: One platter of minced pigeon with shrimp crackers, enough for four as an appetizer or snack.
chim-cau-bam-xuc-phong-tom.description: Minced pigeon is quickly stir-fried with shallots, garlic, chili, onion and Vietnamese coriander. Crisp shrimp crackers scoop up the aromatic, tender meat; Bếp Việt uses boneless meat for a family-friendly version.
chim-cau-bam-xuc-phong-tom.finished_dish: The pigeon is browned but not dry, the Vietnamese coriander remains fragrant and the seasoning is balanced; the crackers stay crisp at serving.
chim-cau-bam-xuc-phong-tom.serving: Serve the hot pigeon mixture in a shallow bowl, topped with roasted peanuts and fried shallots. Keep the fried crackers separate for scooping.
tips: Remove all small bones and mince the meat separately; do not mince bones into the dish.
Stir-fry over high heat and work in batches if needed so the meat browns instead of stewing.
Add Vietnamese coriander and scallions at the end and toss briefly to preserve their aroma.
Fry the shrimp crackers in properly heated oil and drain before serving.
search_terms: chim cau bam xuc phong shrimp
chim-cau-bam-xuc-phong-tom.image_alt: A savory plate of minced pigeon stir-fried with aromatics, served with crisp shrimp crackers.
chim-cau-bam-xuc-phong-tom.time_note: About 45 minutes including cleaning, deboning and quick stir-frying.

ingredients.name: Young pigeons
ingredients.notes: Clean, remove meat from the bones and mince coarsely; reserve bones for stock if desired.

ingredients.name: Shrimp crackers
ingredients.notes: Fry until crisp or use ready-fried crackers.

ingredients.name: Dried shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Finely chop.

ingredients.name: Red chili
ingredients.notes: Remove seeds for less heat and dice.

ingredients.name: Vietnamese coriander
ingredients.notes: Wash and roughly chop.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Slice, separating the white ends.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: Finely dice.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add gradually to taste.

ingredients.name: Oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Adds a rounded savory flavor.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Optional; reduce or omit.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use some during cooking and the rest to finish.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Crush coarsely.

ingredients.name: Crispy fried shallots
ingredients.notes: Sprinkle over the dish at serving.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For stir-frying the pigeon.

preparation_steps.instruction: Clean the pigeons, remove all meat from the bones and mince coarsely. Do not mince the bones; reserve them for a separate stock if desired.
Chop the shallots and garlic; dice the chili and onion, slice the scallions and Vietnamese coriander, and crush the peanuts.
Mix the fish sauce with oyster sauce, seasoning powder and pepper. Check the shrimp crackers; if uncooked, prepare a separate pot of oil for frying.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil and saute the shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add the pigeon and stir-fry over high heat until browned and no liquid remains.
Season with the fish-sauce and oyster-sauce mixture. Add the onion and chili and stir-fry briefly until the onion is just tender.
Add the scallions and Vietnamese coriander, toss briefly and turn off the heat. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
If using uncooked crackers, fry a few at a time in hot oil until puffed and crisp, then drain. Serve the hot pigeon with the crackers, peanuts and fried shallots.

chim-cau-bam-xuc-phong-tom.media_alt_text: A savory plate of minced pigeon stir-fried with aromatics, served with crisp shrimp crackers.

vit-om-chuoi-dau.name: Duck Stewed with Green Bananas and Tofu
aliases: Duck with green banana and tofu stew
vit-om-chuoi-dau.serving_basis: About 1.2 kg of duck stewed with green bananas and tofu, serving four.
vit-om-chuoi-dau.description: Duck is marinated with ginger, lemongrass and simple seasonings, then simmered until tender with green bananas and golden fried tofu. The bananas turn mellow, the tofu absorbs the savory broth and the duck stays aromatic.
vit-om-chuoi-dau.finished_dish: The duck is tender but not falling apart, the bananas are soft and intact, and the golden tofu has absorbed the lightly thickened broth.
vit-om-chuoi-dau.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice or fresh rice vermicelli, making sure each portion includes duck, banana and tofu.
tips: Rub the duck with ginger and rice wine, rinse and pat dry to reduce its strong aroma.
After peeling, soak the green bananas in lightly salted water to limit discoloration.
Simmer the duck until nearly tender before adding bananas; add tofu near the end to keep it intact.
Once the bananas are added, simmer gently and stir carefully.
dish_type: Duck, green banana and tofu stew
vit-om-chuoi-dau.image_alt: Duck gently stewed with green bananas and golden fried tofu in a savory broth.
vit-om-chuoi-dau.time_note: About 115 minutes including 30 minutes of marinating; older duck or larger pieces may need longer simmering.

ingredients.name: Duck pieces
ingredients.notes: Use cleaned duck cut into serving pieces.

ingredients.name: Green bananas
ingredients.notes: Peel, cut into chunks and soak in lightly salted water.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Cut into cubes and fry until golden before stewing.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Bruise the stalks and mince the tender part.

ingredients.name: Small shallots
ingredients.notes: Crush or mince.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Use half for cleaning and slice the rest.

ingredients.name: Rice wine
ingredients.notes: Use to clean the duck and reduce odor.

ingredients.name: Turmeric powder
ingredients.notes: Adds a light golden tone; optional.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add gradually depending on saltiness.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Reserve some for the marinade.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the savory seasoning and lemongrass.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use part of it in the marinade.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For searing the duck and aromatics.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually to make the braising liquid; adjust as needed.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rub the duck with crushed ginger and rice wine, rinse, cut into serving pieces and pat dry.
Marinate the duck with fish sauce, salt, sugar, pepper and turmeric for about 30 minutes. Bruise the lemongrass and shallots; peel and cut the bananas and soak them in lightly salted water.
Cube the tofu and fry until golden on all sides. Slice the remaining ginger into thin strips.

cooking_steps.instruction: Heat the oil and saute lemongrass, shallots and ginger until fragrant. Add the duck and sear until firm and opaque on the surface.
Add enough water to nearly cover the duck, cover and simmer gently for 35–45 minutes until nearly tender; skim any foam.
Add the green bananas and simmer for about 10 minutes. When they are nearly tender, add the fried tofu and adjust the fish sauce and salt.
Simmer a few more minutes so the tofu absorbs the broth. Turn off the heat when the duck is tender but still holds its shape; serve hot with rice or vermicelli.

vit-om-chuoi-dau.media_alt_text: Duck gently stewed with green bananas and golden fried tofu in a savory broth.

canh-ga-dau-trang-khoai-mon.name: Chicken Soup with White Beans and Taro
aliases: Chicken soup with fresh white beans and taro
White bean and taro chicken soup
canh-ga-dau-trang-khoai-mon.serving_basis: A soup pot with 500 g chicken thigh, fresh white beans and taro, serving four.
canh-ga-dau-trang-khoai-mon.description: Chicken thigh is lightly seared, then simmered with fresh white beans and taro until tender. The broth is mild and savory, while the beans and taro make this an easy, nourishing family soup.
canh-ga-dau-trang-khoai-mon.finished_dish: The chicken is tender, the white beans soft but intact and the taro mellow without dissolving; the light broth is fragrant with scallion and sawtooth coriander.
canh-ga-dau-trang-khoai-mon.serving: Serve hot with chopped scallion and sawtooth coriander, alongside steamed rice. Adjust the seasoning at the end to keep the broth gentle.
tips: Use fresh white beans; if substituting dried beans, soak and pre-cook them until tender first.
Sear the chicken briefly to firm its surface; it does not need to brown deeply.
Cut the taro into even pieces and stir gently to keep it intact.
Skim the broth early and season gradually.
dish_type: Chicken, white bean and taro soup
search_terms: canh chicken dau trang khoai mon
canh-ga-dau-trang-khoai-mon.image_alt: A bowl of chicken soup with white beans, taro and a clear savory broth.
canh-ga-dau-trang-khoai-mon.time_note: About 80 minutes including 15 minutes of marinating; fresh white beans keep the cooking time shorter.

ingredients.name: Chicken thigh
ingredients.notes: Cut into even bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Fresh white beans
ingredients.notes: Shell and rinse; do not use dried beans unless they have been soaked.

ingredients.name: Taro
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into medium cubes.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Chop for garnish.

ingredients.name: Sawtooth coriander
ingredients.notes: Wash and chop.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For searing the chicken.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Adjust to control the broth strength.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Divide between the marinade and soup.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Add at the end if needed.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use some for the chicken and the rest at serving.

preparation_steps.instruction: Rinse the chicken thigh, cut into bite-size pieces and marinate with some seasoning powder and pepper for 15 minutes.
Shell and rinse the fresh white beans. Peel and cube the taro; wash and chop the scallion and sawtooth coriander.
Heat the oil in a pan and quickly sear the chicken on all sides until firm, then remove.

cooking_steps.instruction: Put the chicken and white beans in a pot with the water. Bring to a gentle boil, skim the foam and simmer for about 15 minutes.
Add the taro and cook for another 15–20 minutes until the chicken, beans and taro are just tender; stir gently to prevent the taro from breaking.
Season with the remaining seasoning powder and fish sauce to taste. Turn off the heat, add scallion, sawtooth coriander and pepper, then serve hot.

canh-ga-dau-trang-khoai-mon.media_alt_text: A bowl of chicken soup with white beans, taro and a clear savory broth.
